title: System Diagnostics with Severity
description: Analyze our ship systems. Report on 3 different systems using appropriate log levels. Show me you can communicate priority—what's working, what's concerning, what's critical.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Good, but you're sending everything at the same priority. Not all messages are equal—learn to indicate severity. Some systems are fine, some have warnings, some are critical."
story.context: The ship has multiple system states. Log levels help prioritize what to fix first. INFO for normal status, WARN for potential issues, ERROR for critical problems.

theory.title: Log Levels and Message Severity
theory.content:
\n\n
\n\n

MENTOR-9 pulls up the ship's log display. It's cluttered with hundreds of messages—all appearing equally important.

This is chaos, PROTO-7. We need to prioritize. That's where log levels come in.

Understanding Log Levels

When your ship's computer talks to you, not every message has the same urgency. Some are routine status updates. Others are warnings. Some scream fix this NOW! Log levels let you tag each message with its importance.

Think of it like a triage system. You have several priority levels:

  • INFO - Everything's normal, routine status updates
  • WARN - Something's not quite right, but not critical
  • ERROR - Serious problem that needs immediate attention
  • DEBUG - Detailed technical information for troubleshooting
  • TRACE - Very detailed debugging information

In the log report, different levels appear in different colors, making critical issues instantly visible.

How to Add Log Levels

The syntax is simple—just add the level after your message:

*** Test Cases ***
Ship Status
    Log    Navigation online    INFO
    Log    Hull breach in sector 7    WARN
    Log    Life support failing    ERROR

If you don't specify a level, Robot Framework uses INFO by default.

When to Use Each Level

Here's a quick guide:

  • INFO: Normal operations, things working as expected, progress updates
  • WARN: Something's off but the system keeps running, degraded performance, things to investigate later
  • ERROR: Critical problems, system failures, things that need fixing right now
  • DEBUG: Technical details helpful during development and troubleshooting
  • TRACE: Very verbose output for deep debugging (rarely used)
